finding.title: restoreBackup / config rollback silently DESTROYS all provider API keys (APIKeyEnc lost by json:"-", then provider table wiped and recreated without it)
finding.evidence: bundle.go:81-93 — RestoreBundle first wipes the provider table `if err := tx.Where("1 = 1").Delete(table).Error; err != nil {` (table list line 82 includes `&model.Provider{}`) then recreates providers with `if len(b.Providers) > 0 { if err := tx.Create(&b.Providers).Error`. But the bundle JSON never contains the ciphertext: model.go:107 `APIKeyEnc    string    `gorm:"type:text" json:"-"` // AES-GCM 加密存储 (REQ-005 ④)` — so every JSON.Marshal of ConfigBundle (backup.go:31 `body, _ := json.Marshal(b)`, configstatus.go:68 `body, _ := json.MarshalIndent(b, "", "  ")`, runtime/manager.go:386 `if b, err := json.Marshal(bundle); err == nil {` for ConfigVersion snapshots) drops it, contradicting bundle.go:15 comment `// ConfigBundle 可序列化的全量配置（密钥保持 DB 原样密文，跨版本/备份一致）。`. runtime/manager.go:214-218: `if plain, err := m.enc.Decrypt(p.APIKeyEnc); err == nil { ... } else { p.APIKey = "" // 解密失败：保留空密钥，该上游调用时会失败 }` — empty APIKeyEnc fails decrypt, so after any restore/rollback every upstream is called with no credential. Meanwhile APIKeyMasked (model.go:109, `json:"api_key_masked"`) DOES round-trip, so the admin UI still displays a masked key and the wipe looks healthy.
finding.impact: Every use of the two safety nets (POST /backups/restore — even restoring a legitimately created backup by ID — and POST /config/rollback) hard-deletes and recreates every provider row without its encrypted API key. All gateway traffic then authenticates to upstream providers with empty keys (upstream 401s), and the loss is unrecoverable from any backup or snapshot because no copy of APIKeyEnc ever existed in the JSON. The masked-key display hides the damage.
finding.mitigations_checked: Gateway API keys are NOT destroyed: ConfigBundle.APIKeys (bundle.go:24) is parsed but RestoreBundle never touches api_keys; KeyHash is json:"-" (model.go:37). api_key_masked being the only key material in backups means backups do not exfiltrate provider credentials (positive).
finding.recommendation: Include APIKeyEnc in a dedicated bundle struct (kept out of HTTP list responses) so it round-trips; or make RestoreBundle preserve existing APIKeyEnc on recreate (upsert / re-read ciphertext by provider ID) and refuse restore/rollback that would blank credentials. Add a test asserting provider count AND non-empty APIKeyEnc after a restore cycle.

reason:
CONFIRMED. I read every cited file end-to-end and each verbatim quote is exact and at the stated line; the whole chain reproduces from code alone, and I found four corroborating facts the original auditor did not cite.

QUOTE / LINE VERIFICATION (all exact, no wrong-line defect):
- backend/internal/runtime/bundle.go:86 `if err := tx.Where("1 = 1").Delete(table).Error; err != nil {`; the table list at bundle.go:81-85 starts `&model.Provider{}, &model.AliasUpstream{}, &model.ModelAlias{},`; recreate at bundle.go:90-91 `if len(b.Providers) > 0 {` / `if err := tx.Create(&b.Providers).Error; err != nil {`. Cited primary line 86 is the destructive statement, so the pin is correct (the loss itself is the Create at line 91; both are inside the same tx).
- bundle.go:15 comment `// ConfigBundle 可序列化的全量配置（密钥保持 DB 原样密文，跨版本/备份一致）。` and bundle.go:24 `APIKeys    []model.APIKey        `json:"api_keys"`` — verbatim.
- model.go:107 `APIKeyEnc    string    `gorm:"type:text" json:"-"` // AES-GCM 加密存储 (REQ-005 ④)`; model.go:109 `APIKeyMasked string    `gorm:"size:64" json:"api_key_masked"``; model.go:37 `KeyHash   string    `gorm:"size:64;index" json:"-"` // sha256(hex)` — verbatim.
- runtime/manager.go:214-218 exactly as quoted (line 216 additionally does `p.APIKeyEnc = ""`, an in-memory redaction only, and line 218 `p.APIKey = "" // 解密失败：保留空密钥，该上游调用时会失败`); manager.go:386 `if b, err := json.Marshal(bundle); err == nil {` inside recordVersion (389-391) which writes ConfigVersion.SnapshotJSON.
- PATH CORRECTION (immaterial to the verdict): the evidence writes `backup.go:31` and `configstatus.go:68` as if under a handler/ directory; no `backend/internal/handler/` exists. Actual: backend/internal/admin/backup.go:31 `body, _ := json.Marshal(b)` and backend/internal/admin/configstatus.go:68 `body, _ := json.MarshalIndent(b, "", "  ")`; rollbackConfig really is admin/configstatus.go:52-60; restore really is admin/backup.go:56-88 (`if err := s.mgr.RestoreBundle(b); err != nil {` at line 81). All line numbers still match exactly.

CHAIN, LINK BY LINK:
1) Both entry points are admin-authenticated and unauthenticated-free of any second factor/role gate: routes.go:139 `api.POST("/config/rollback", s.AuthMiddleware(), s.rollbackConfig)` and routes.go:147 `api.POST("/backups/restore", s.AuthMiddleware(), s.restoreBackup)`; admin/middleware.go:14-33 only validates the Bearer JWT and sets operator/userID — there is no RBAC anywhere, so any valid admin session can call them.
2) Rollback is reachable in practice: bundle.go:146-153 needs >=2 status='ok' ConfigVersion rows and every reload writes one (manager.go:389-391), so any deployed instance qualifies. Restore qualifies with any content, including a backup the system itself just created (admin/backup.go:25-43 -> json.Marshal of ExportBundle -> restoreBackup by ID, backup.go:66-75 `data = r.Content`).
3) The bundle really has no ciphertext: Provider.APIKeyEnc is json:"-" and I confirmed there is no custom MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON and no alternate bundle/export struct that carries it — a repo-wide grep for `api_key_enc|MarshalJSON|UnmarshalJSON|api_key_masked` returns only model.go:109, frontend/src/api/types.ts:166 and frontend/src/pages/providers/Providers.tsx:246. ExportBundle (bundle.go:32 `if err := m.db.Find(&b.Providers).Error; err != nil {`) loads the ciphertext into the Go struct, so the loss happens at Marshal, not at load — exactly what the finding says.
4) The wipe is a HARD delete: Provider (model.go:102-114) has no gorm.DeletedAt and repo-wide grep for `DeletedAt|BeforeCreate|AfterSave|Callback` finds no GORM hooks or soft-delete config, so line 86 removes the row and line 91 re-inserts it with APIKeyEnc = '' (GORM Create emits all columns; the row is new anyway).
5) Decryption of the empty value fails as claimed: crypto/crypto.go:43-51 `raw, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(enc)` succeeds for "" and then `if len(raw) < ns { return "", errors.New("ciphertext too short") }` returns an error, so manager.go:218 sets p.APIKey = "" and the provider is still published into the snapshot (manager.go:244-246 builds ResolvedUpstream{... APIKey: p.APIKey ...}) because only `!ok || !p.Enabled` filters upstreams (manager.go:236-239).
6) Total outage: gateway.go:507 `req, err := adapter.BuildUpstreamRequest(up.Protocol, cr, up.UpstreamModel, up.BaseURL, up.APIKey)` with no empty-key guard, and adapter.go:560 `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)` / adapter.go:679 `req.Header.Set("x-api-key", apiKey)` send an empty credential. Enabled round-trips, so routing continues and every model fails upstream. Both Reload and Bump fire right after: backup.go:86 `s.mgr.Bump()` and bundle.go:165-166 `m.Bump()` / `_ = m.Reload("rollback")`.

NEW CORROBORATION I verified (strengthens, does not weaken, the finding):
- The rest of the codebase deliberately maintains the invariant that restore violates. providers.go:111-119 `if req.APIKey != "" {` guards the update path so an admin cannot blank APIKeyEnc by omission, and providers.go:137-141 `s.db.Model(&model.AliasUpstream{}).Where("provider_id = ?", id).Count(&count)` / `if count > 0 { s.fail(c, 409, 40901, "该供应商仍被模型别名引用，无法删除")` blocks deleting a provider that is in use. So for providers referenced by aliases, restoring/rolling back is the ONLY code path in the product that can erase a credential — the actor does not already hold that specific power.
- The damage really is masked: listProviders (providers.go:34-45) returns DB rows, APIKeyMasked round-trips (model.go:109) and is what the UI renders (Providers.tsx:246 dataIndex: 'api_key_masked'), so the console still shows a plausible masked key. Worse, the health probe cannot detect it: health.go:116-125 `if p.APIKeyEnc == "" { return "" }` sends no Authorization and health.go's own doc (lines 4-6) states `任何 HTTP 响应（含 401/403/404）= 端点可达 = 健康`, so upstream_health stays green on a 401 (health.go:106-113 `c.bl.RecordSuccess(p.ID)`).
- Nothing retains a recoverable copy: audit.LogOp (audit.go:109-123) serializes before/after with `json.Marshal` (line 114), so OperationLog BeforeJSON/AfterJSON, ConfigVersion.SnapshotJSON and BackupRecord.Content all exclude APIKeyEnc. "Unrecoverable from any backup or snapshot" is accurate; recovery means retyping every key.
- No test covers it (grep for `func Test.*(Backup|Bundle|Rollback|Restore)` -> none), and no doc acknowledges it, while bundle.go:15 asserts the opposite intent — so this is a genuine defect, not a documented design choice.

PRECISION CORRECTIONS TO THE IMPACT TEXT (do not change severity): (a) the operations ARE recorded in the audit log as action=restore (backup.go:85, before/after nil) and action=rollback (configstatus.go:58), so "records no evidence" should read "records the action but no before/after state"; (b) the outage is not silent to traffic — clients get upstream errors and CallLog rows — it is the *cause* that is hidden; (c) rollback uses a Popconfirm whose copy actively misleads (frontend/src/i18n/locales/en-US/pages/configStatus.ts:9 `This restores the previous version of all provider/model/guardrail/quota config. Continue?`) and does not warn about credentials.

SEVERITY: high stands. It is not critical (no unauth access, no authz bypass, no exfil — the json:"-" exclusion actually prevents credential leakage in exports, correctly noted as a positive by the filer). It is above medium: it is an authed-but-severe integrity/availability failure — mass, silent, permanent loss of every upstream credential, with both designed recovery mechanisms converted into the destruction vector. The privilege delta over normal admin CRUD (which is explicitly prevented from blanking or deleting in-use provider keys) is the justification for keeping high rather than medium. Domain label 'authz' is a stretch — the honest category is data-integrity/availability reachable only by an authenticated admin — but mislabeling the domain is not grounds for refutation since the code, impact and citations all hold.
exploit_sketch:
Precondition: a valid admin JWT (any admin user — there is no RBAC; admin/middleware.go:14-33 only checks the Bearer token). No CSRF/CORS nuance is needed; this is an authenticated, intentional-looking action.

Variant A — the built-in one-click 'safety net' (config rollback):
1. Any instance that has reloaded config twice already qualifies, because manager.go:389-391 writes a ConfigVersion row per reload and bundle.go:151-153 only needs two ok rows.
2. POST /api/admin/v1/config/rollback HTTP/1.1\nAuthorization: Bearer <admin-jwt>\nContent-Type: application/json\n\n{}
3. bundle.go:86 executes DELETE FROM providers WHERE 1=1; bundle.go:91 re-INSERTs every provider with api_key_enc = '' (the snapshot JSON parsed at bundle.go:156 came from a Marshal that dropped the column).
4. bundle.go:165-166 Bump+Reload -> manager.go:214-218 decrypt of '' errors (crypto.go:50 'ciphertext too short') -> Provider.APIKey='' -> ResolvedUpstream.APIKey='' (manager.go:244-246).
5. Every subsequent gateway call — POST /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/messages — forwards with header `Authorization: Bearer ` (adapter.go:560) or `x-api-key: ` (adapter.go:679) -> upstream 401/403 for all models. Dashboard/health still reports upstreams healthy (health.go:4-6 'any HTTP response incl. 401 = healthy') and GET /api/admin/v1/providers still shows api_key_masked, so operators look at the wrong layer.

Variant B — the backup feature (works even on a single-reload instance, and is the operator's documented recovery path):
1. POST /api/admin/v1/backups (admin/backup.go:25-43) -> BackupRecord.Content = json.Marshal(ExportBundle) — no api_key_enc anywhere.
2. POST /api/admin/v1/backups/restore with {"id": <just-created-id>} (backup.go:66-72 `data = r.Content`) — i.e. a perfectly normal 'restore the backup I just took' flow, or {"content": <any exported config.json>}.
3. RestoreBundle (backup.go:81) wipes and recreates providers with blank ciphertext; backup.go:86 Bump() reloads; same outage as above.
4. Recovery attempt fails closed: re-restoring any other backup or rolling back any snapshot re-applies a JSON that also lacks api_key_enc (backup.go:31, configstatus.go:68, manager.go:386, audit.go:114) — the only fix is manually retyping every provider key.

Bonus for a hostile admin: the same primitive is a *stealthy* sabotage/cover-your-tracks tool — the wipe is attributed to an ordinary 'restore'/'rollback' audit entry with before=nil/after=nil (backup.go:85), the UI keeps showing masked keys, and health checks stay green.
checks_performed: Read backend/internal/admin/backup.go + backend/internal/admin/configstatus.go (finding's 'handler/' paths do not exist)
Read backend/internal/runtime/manager.go (436 lines) end-to-end; verified recordVersion snapshot marshalling
Read backend/internal/admin/providers.go (378 lines): empty-api_key guard (111) and delete-blocked-while-referenced (137-141)
Read backend/internal/health/health.go (126 lines): 401 counted as healthy -> damage is invisible to health checks
Read backend/internal/admin/middleware.go + routes.go: both endpoints need only a valid admin JWT, no RBAC
Read backend/internal/crypto/crypto.go: Decrypt("") -> error 'ciphertext too short' (line 50)
Read backend/internal/audit/audit.go LogOp: json.Marshal -> no ciphertext in operation logs either (no recovery copy)
grep api_key_enc|MarshalJSON|UnmarshalJSON -> no custom marshaller, no alternate bundle struct carrying ciphertext
grep DeletedAt|BeforeCreate|AfterSave|Callback -> no GORM hooks, delete is hard
grep adapter Authorization/x-api-key -> empty key is forwarded verbatim, no fail-closed guard
grep func Test.*(Backup|Bundle|Rollback|Restore) -> zero regression tests for this path
grep rollback in frontend -> Popconfirm exists but its copy promises restoration and never mentions credentials
positives_confirmed: Provider credentials are NOT exfiltrated by backups/exports/audit logs (json:"-" on APIKeyEnc) — the leak-free-by-omission property the filer flagged as positive is real and applies to admin/backup.go:45-54 downloadBackup as well

Gateway API keys survive restore: RestoreBundle (bundle.go:79-143) never writes api_keys, so ConfigBundle.APIKeys is inert (a separate restore-completeness gap, not a credential-destruction one) and Quota/RateLimitRule api_key_id references (model.go:179, model.go:197) stay valid; KeyHash is json:"-" (model.go:37) so exported backups also omit gateway key hashes
